allow_large: The owner asked for the v1.2.0 release on 2026-09-29 once all stories were done; a version bump touches the version, the pin and their tests
done_when: Forge's version is 1.2.0 everywhere it is recorded (the package version, this repo's forge.toml pin, and the tests that track the current version), so the v1.2.0 tag installs as 1.2.0

findings.body: This branch changes the Mac installer to request `@v1.2.0`; the Windows installer and README install command now do the same. The release-order ruling explicitly requires these paths to stay on v1.1.0 until the v1.2.0 tag exists. A user running either installer after this branch merges but before tagging will get a failed Forge installation. Revert these three install references for this change.
findings.title: Keep install instructions on v1.1.0 until the v1.2.0 tag exists

why: Clients pin Forge v1.1.0, but main has the prototype, salesperson, live-app, aha, cold-read loop, short plan, upgrade and merge-switch work since then
